title: How to tension fabric in a cross-stitch hoop
subtitle: Mounting fabric taut and keeping tension even while stitching
excerpt: A hoop that is too loose lets the fabric shift with each stitch so the crosses pull into the fabric at an angle instead of lying flat. A hoop that is too tight distorts the Aida squares and makes the holes hard to see. The right tension is drum-tight but not stretched: the fabric should ring faintly if you tap it with a fingertip.
sourceNotes: Hoop mounting practice for counted cross-stitch. Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.

content.text: correctly means keeping the fabric square in the hoop at consistent tension throughout the project. Aida has a natural stiffness that helps it stay taut, but the hoop screw must be tight enough to prevent the fabric slipping as the needle passes through.
Loosen the screw on the outer ring until the two rings separate easily. Lay the inner ring flat on a clean surface and centre the fabric over it, design-area centred in the ring.

Press the outer ring down over the inner ring, sandwiching the fabric between them. The outer ring's screw should be at the top of the hoop as you work; this keeps the screw mechanism away from the stitching area.

Tighten the screw to the point where the fabric is firm in the hoop, then pull the fabric margin gently on all four sides to even out the tension. The Aida grid should run in straight horizontal and vertical lines, not at a diagonal. If the grid has pulled diagonal, loosen and re-mount.

Tighten the screw fully. Tap the centre of the mounted fabric with one fingertip. It should feel firm and give a faint ring or vibration, like a stretched skin. If it feels soft, tighten more. If the fabric has pulled into a diagonal wave, loosen, reposition, and re-tighten.
Check the tension again after the first few stitches. Heavy needle passes can loosen the grip of the hoop. Tighten the screw as needed during stitching.

items.symptom: The fabric keeps slipping in the hoop
items.cause: The hoop is too large for the fabric tension, or the inner ring is smooth and provides no grip.
items.fix: Wrap the inner ring with a strip of cotton twill tape or bias binding before mounting the fabric. The wrapped ring grips the Aida more firmly. Alternatively, use a hoop with a tightening mechanism rather than a plain sliding hoop.

items.symptom: The Aida squares are distorted after mounting
items.cause: The outer ring went on at an angle, or the fabric was pulled unevenly when tightening.
items.fix: Loosen the hoop, reposition the fabric so the grid lines run square to the hoop axis, and remount. Always pull the fabric gently on all four sides before tightening fully.

content.text: Remove the hoop at the end of each stitching session to prevent hoop marks. Store the piece in a bag or rolled loosely in a clean cloth. Re-mounting each time only takes a minute and protects the fabric from permanent ring impressions.
